course: Ders içeriği gereği çok kalabalık olduğundan kronolojik olarakta takip etsek eksik kalmaktadır. Ders iki bölüme ayrılırsa hem öğrenciler için daha efektif hem de öğretmenler için ödevlendirmesi daha kolay olacaktır. Dersi anlamak için çok sayıda film izlemek gerekli ve her öğrencinin hazır bulunuşu aynı değil. Ben sinemaya ilgi duyduğumdan dersi takip etmekte zorlanmadım ama ilgisi düşük seviyede veya hiç olmayan bir öğrencinin bu dersten verim olması mümkün değildir. Derste yakın dönem sinema hakkında hiç konuşamadık ki bence bu durum golden age ten french new wave'e veya greek weird wave den bugüne bağlantı kurmak için gereklidir. Yönetmenler üzerinden dersleri takip etmeye zaman kalmadı. Kubrick, Scorsese, Varda, Pasolini, Fellini ve daha nice isimden bahsedemedik en üzücü olan 2000li yönetmenleri sinemasına hiç eğilememiş olmamız. Ders iki bölüm olarak verilirse hem öğrencilerin filmleri takip edebilmesi için tevşik edecek aynı zamanda sinema kuramlarını ilk kaynaklarından okumak için zamanımız olacaktır.

Ufuk Hoca is clearly knowledgeable and competent in his field. However, I do not think these strengths are fully reflected in the feedback we receive during project critiques. Since the course is taught together with Andreas Hoca, Andreas tends to dominate the discussions while Ufuk Hoca remains more in the background. Because of this, especially in projects involving sound design, I feel that many areas that could be improved are left unresolved or not discussed deeply enough. I understand that both instructors are trying to renew the curriculum and introduce different approaches to the department. However, I think trying to achieve this by completely disregarding what previous semesters built, and by giving feedback in areas where they themselves may not yet have enough expertise, especially in the TouchDesigner project, creates an inconsistent learning environment.

I would also like to comment on Andreas Hoca’s approach. While some of his feedback can be constructive, there are also moments where the comments become too personal and disconnected from the course itself. Frankly, I find this outside the level of professionalism that the department aims to represent. When working hard on our projects, I would rather receive no feedback at all than feedback that feels overly individualized in an unproductive way. Overall, I believe the department and the instructors need a clearer long-term direction regarding the curriculum and should apply it consistently for several years. Making major changes every semester, testing them on students, and still expecting professional-level outcomes seriously affects the quality of the results and leaves students feeling uncertain about the direction of the course.

course:
The most positive aspect of the course was that it challenged us with unfamiliar projects and pushed us to adapt to difficult situations. However, beyond that, I struggled to find many positive sides to the experience. Our first major assignment was a “living music video” project in TouchDesigner, a program that most of us had no experience with. While the concept initially sounded interesting, the process quickly became frustrating because we lacked both technical knowledge and proper guidance. When we asked questions, the answers were often simply “ask GPT,” and even then the responses we received were usually not helpful. At some point, the project stopped feeling educational and became more exhausting than productive. I believe education should involve learning from experienced people, not only receiving feedback after struggling alone.

Another major issue was the inconsistency throughout the semester. The department emphasizes solving problems independently, but when we genuinely tried to learn the correct approaches, there was rarely clear guidance available. At the same time, expectations for project quality remained very high, which made the uncertainty stressful for both individuals and teams. Later in the semester, we were suddenly given a second film option instead of another TouchDesigner project, and we mainly chose it to avoid TouchDesigner rather than out of genuine interest. We wanted more varied and real-world-oriented projects like the music video and documentary assignments from previous semesters. Overall, the constant changes and unclear direction made the semester discouraging. At times, there are constant changes and new ideas, but the long-term direction and results remain unclear. Despite all of this, being able to complete both projects still felt like a major achievement fort us.

The strongest is that we had two choices to choose from for our final project. The weakest is that AGAIN no industry-based work has been encouraged to make. Everything HAS to be experimental or something.
assistant: Regarding the assistant support, I unfortunately did not find the experience very helpful. The assistant who was presented as knowledgeable in TouchDesigner often gave responses that felt unrelated to the actual questions we were asking. Because of this, we still had to solve most of the technical problems on our own. I understand that not every issue can be solved immediately, but in a course built around a highly technical and unfamiliar program, clearer and more solution-oriented support would have made a significant difference. I hope future semesters work with assistants who are better prepared to respond directly and effectively to students’ questions.
